cards.explanation: The disciples rub the heads of grain in their hands and eat them. Luke 6:1 says the disciples "…began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them." No oven, no timer, no cooling rack. Just hands and a walk through a field. I've baked a lot of batches, friends, and even I have never made a snack that fast.

The Pharisees ask why the disciples are doing what's unlawful on the Sabbath. In Luke 6:2 they say, "Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?" Their question is about the day. Not the field, not the grain, just what's happening on the Sabbath.

The answer is True, and it's right there in Luke 6:4: David "…entered the house of God…" He did this when he and his companions were hungry. Jesus brings up that moment after some of the Pharisees ask their question about the Sabbath. I'd say Jesus really did bring the receipts.

The word is bread. Luke 6:4 says David "…took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions…" He didn't keep it all to himself, he shared it. Consecrated means set apart, so this wasn't ordinary bread off the counter.

Only the priests were allowed to eat it. Luke 6:4 says David "…ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat." That's what makes Jesus' example so striking, friends. The bread was set apart for the priests, and David ate it anyway.

Jesus says the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath. His words are, "The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath." (Luke 6:5). Lord means He has authority over the day. After a debate about what's lawful, that's a big thing to say.

The scribes and Pharisees are waiting to see if Jesus will heal on the Sabbath. Luke 6:7 says they were "…watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath." They were looking for a reason to accuse Him. I think that's the longest stare in the whole synagogue.

Jesus tells the man, "Get up and stand among us." That's Luke 6:8, and the man "…got up and stood there." Jesus does this knowing their thoughts, while the scribes and Pharisees are watching Him closely. I think the man needed some courage right then.

The two words are evil and destroy. Jesus asks, "…which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?" (Luke 6:9). Good and evil are set side by side, and so are save life and destroy. He asks it right in front of them, friends, and it leaves no room to hide.

Jesus tells the man, "Stretch out your hand." After looking around at all of them, He says it to the man in Luke 6:10. A withered hand, and a command to stretch it out. That's a lot to ask, and I think it took some faith.
The answer is False. Jesus says, "Stretch out your hand." and Luke 6:10 says, "He did so, and it was restored." The man doesn't refuse. He does it, and his hand is made whole.
The word is rage. Luke 6:11 says the scribes and Pharisees "…were filled with rage…" A man's hand was just restored, and this is how they react. I think this part is heavy.
The answer is True. Luke 6:11 says the scribes and Pharisees "…began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus." They talk it over together. The story isn't over, friends.
